I. Increasing the clock cycle rate  
→ Higher clock rate means fewer cycles per second (higher frequency), so each instruction takes less time. Since CPI is constant, increasing the clock rate reduces the time per instruction, thus reducing total execution time.

→ Forwarding is used to avoid stalls when data dependencies occur. Disallowing forwarding means more stalls will occur when instructions depend on results of previous instructions. This increases the number of cycles per instruction (even if CPI is the same, stalls add cycles), so execution time increases.  
❌ This does *not* improve execution time.
